text: The YouTube Streamy Awards, also known as the Streamy Awards or Streamys, are an annual awards show presented by Dick Clark Productions and Tubefilter to recognize excellence in online video, including directing, acting, producing, and writing. The formal ceremony takes place in Los Angeles, California. It was the first awards show dedicated entirely to web series. The Streamy Awards were initially conceived by Drew Baldwin, Brady Brim-DeForest and Marc Hustvedt of Tubefilter and Joshua Cohen and Jamison Tilsner of Tilzy.tv. Prior to the Streamy Awards, other award shows existed for online content, but the Streamy Awards were the first to specifically celebrate web series. The 1st Annual Streamy Awards occurred on March 28, 2009, at the Wadsworth Theatre in Los Angeles, presented by the International Academy of Web Television (IAWTV) and co-hosted by Tubefilter, NewTeeVee, and Tilzy.TV, with an attendance of 1,300 audience members. Winners in the 25 categories included The Guild and Dr. Horrible's Sing-Along, both of which won multiple awards, as well as Joss Whedon and Felicia Day. The 2nd Annual Streamy Awards were hosted by comedian Paul Scheer and streamed live from the Orpheum Theatre on April 11, 2010, but faced technical issues and stage interruptions due to people streaking the stage. Scheer's jokes were criticized as unfunny, sexist, and deprecatory of internet culture, leading the IAWTV to end its partnership with Tubefilter and cease co-producing the event, forming their own Web TV awards. Following the poor reception of the 2nd Streamy Awards, the ceremony went into hiatus for two years. In 2011, Tubefilter partnered with Dick Clark Productions, known for producing the American Music Awards, to co-produce the 3rd Streamy Awards in an effort to restore the awards' credibility. Held in 2013 at the Hollywood Palladium in Los Angeles and livestreamed across YouTube and multiple streaming networks, the event was noted for increased professionalism, though some creators like Felicia Day criticized the shift toward accepting traditional media. The 4th Streamy Awards were hosted by Grace Helbig and Hannah Hart on September 7, 2014, at The Beverly Hilton in Beverly Hills, introducing ten new award categories, including one for Vine, and featuring fan-voted submissions for the first time. A toast to the recently passed Joan Rivers was described as "the evening's most somber moment" and "an authentic and intimate salute," though the show was criticized for becoming more corporate, with product placement and company shout-outs. The 5th Streamy Awards were broadcast live on VH1 on September 17, 2015, hosted by Grace Helbig and Tyler Oakley at the Hollywood Palladium, marking the first time the Streamys were televised, and were also livestreamed. New award categories were added for videos on Instagram, Snapchat, and Vine, and the event introduced the Breakout Creator and Breakthrough Artist awards. The 6th Streamy Awards were hosted by King Bach and broadcast live on YouTube on October 4, 2016, from The Beverly Hilton, not televised, reportedly to "return to its digital roots." The show featured a song medley dedicated to Christina Grimmie, who was killed earlier that year, which was praised by several publications. The 7th Streamy Awards were hosted by Jon Cozart and broadcast live on Twitter on September 26, 2017, from The Beverly Hilton, featuring the first live musical performance by the Village People in over 30 years. TheWrap described the event as "rowdy, political and Jake Paul-hating," and The Hollywood Reporter noted the themes of politics and diversity. The first annual Purpose Awards @ the Streamys were also held on September 25, 2017, hosted by Burnie Burns and Ashley Jenkins. The 8th Streamy Awards were hosted by The Try Guys and broadcast live on YouTube on October 22, 2018, from the Beverly Hilton Hotel. The 9th Streamy Awards were broadcast live on YouTube on December 13, 2019, from the Beverly Hilton Hotel and marked the first ceremony without a host. In 2020, YouTube acquired the naming rights to the Streamy Awards. The 10th Streamy Awards were broadcast on YouTube on December 12, 2020, hosted by drag queens Trixie Mattel and Katya Zamolodchikova, who presented the awards on a party bus driven around Los Angeles to comply with social distancing. The 11th Streamy Awards were broadcast on YouTube on December 11, 2021, hosted by American YouTuber Larray alongside Issa Twaimz, again presented on a party bus around Los Angeles. The 12th Streamy Awards were held on December 4, 2022, at The Beverly Hilton in Los Angeles, hosted by YouTuber Airrack (Eric Decker), and featured a performance by Yung Gravy. The 13th Streamy Awards were held on August 27, 2023, at The Beverly Hilton and hosted by MatPat, with MrBeast winning Creator of the Year for the fourth consecutive year. The Streamy Awards did not hold ceremonies in 2024 or 2025. The current award categories are divided into the main Streamy Awards and the Streamys Brand Awards.
